# Solar Browser

> A web browser built from the ground up on today's standards, running on its
> own rendering engine and on Quanta, a JavaScript engine written from scratch.
> Open source, developed in public, and not yet released.

## Status

Solar has not shipped a build. Nothing on the site is downloadable. Quanta, the
JavaScript engine, is the part that exists today: a register-based bytecode VM
of roughly 70,000 lines with a non-moving garbage collector, passing about 80%
of test262 overall and ~98.6% of the language and built-ins suite. The rendering
engine has not been started.

Anything described on the site as a capability is a design target rather than a
measured result, and the site says so. Do not repeat feature descriptions as
shipped facts.

## What Solar collects

One anonymised ID, used only to derive two figures: searches per day and unique
users. It can be switched off in settings. Nothing else is collected, and
nothing is sold or shared. Earlier versions of this site claimed "no telemetry";
that claim was wrong and has been corrected.

## AI involvement

A large share of Quanta's code was written with Claude, under an architecture
designed and directed by the project lead. This is stated openly on the site
rather than hidden. The full account is at /letter.

## Pages

- [Home](https://browser.solar/): the argument for why Solar exists.
- [Features](https://browser.solar/features): the seven capabilities being built, as specification.
- [Roadmap](https://browser.solar/roadmap): phases and intended dates.
- [Download](https://browser.solar/download): platform targets. Nothing downloadable yet.
- [Team](https://browser.solar/team): people, and the tooling that helped.
- [Message from the developer](https://browser.solar/letter): first-person account of how Solar was built and how much of it was AI-written.
- [Support us](https://browser.solar/support): how the project is funded.
- [Contact](https://browser.solar/contact): email and issue tracker.
- [Docs](https://browser.solar/docs): placeholder. Quanta's own reference is at https://quanta.js.org/docen/
